speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to help me determine the cause, how long has the swelling been present?

Have you experienced any trauma to the knee, or does the pain worsen with specific activities like walking or climbing stairs?

Finally, to better assess your risk of inflammatory conditions, do you have a history of gout, rheumatoid arthritis, or other autoimmune diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular onset).

I am concerned because you mentioned the swelling started after playing without a specific injury, yet your uncle had similar problems. Given his age and the family history, this presentation is classic for early-onset Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis. I will need to request an Ultrasound of the right knee to confirm synovitis before we proceed.
